title: Looker Conversational Analytics: 2027 Token Bill
summary: Looker Conversational Analytics explained: how it depends on LookML, Gemini in Looker features, Data Studio limits and token billing from February 2027.
body_markdown:
*Disclosure: This article is published by Upsolve AI. Where our product appears alongside others, the comparison is based on publicly available information as of November 2026.*


Looker Conversational Analytics is the chat interface inside Looker: a user asks a question in plain English, Gemini picks the LookML fields and filters, and Looker writes the SQL. Usage carries no token charges today, but[that promotion ends on January 31, 2027](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) . From February 1, questions draw on a metered token pool, and archived copies of Google’s pricing page show three different versions of that pool since May.


Two things need checking before then: how much of your LookML the feature can use, and how many tokens your questions consume. The first matters more.


## Key Takeaways


-


**The agent doesn’t write SQL.** It selects fields, filters, sorts and limits, and[Looker composes the query from your LookML](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) . Your governance carries over. So do the gaps in your model.


-


**Billing starts February 1, 2027.** Overage is[$3.00 per 1M input tokens and $20.00 per 1M output tokens](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) . On the assumptions below, an internal team pays tens of dollars a month and a large embedded deployment pays thousands.


-


**Allowances now scale with users.** Each internal user adds 1M input and 20K output tokens, with a floor of 60M and 1.2M per production instance. An Embed customer with few users has far less than the page promised in October.


-


**Looker Studio is now Data Studio, and it’s a different product here.** Its new experience[only chats with BigQuery data agents](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/conversational-analytics-overview) , not Looker Explores.


-


**Native is the right default** if your data is modeled in LookML and your users work in Looker. A dedicated data agent earns its cost when data, users or testing needs sit outside that boundary.


## Looker Conversational Analytics vs the Rest of Gemini in Looker


“Gemini in Looker” is the umbrella.[Conversational Analytics is one feature under it](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/gemini-overview-looker) , and it comes in three forms that behave differently:


-


**Explore conversations:** typically one user, one Explore, no custom context. The[Start a conversation button isn’t available in the new Explore experience](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) .


-


**Explore data agents:** up to five Explores, plus instructions, glossaries and verified queries. They can be shared, and they’re the only form where[verified queries work](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-data-agents) .


-


**Dashboard agents:** one shared agent per dashboard, scoped to it and its query-linked tiles. No Advanced Analytics, and agents on LookML dashboards can’t take custom instructions.

Insight Assistant is a separate feature, yet[System Activity lists it as a surface on the token usage tab](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/system-activity-dashboards) , so include it when you baseline usage.


The mode setting also affects cost.[Google says Thinking mode isn’t more accurate than Fast mode](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-data) ; it spends extra tokens to show the reasoning, and those[thoughts count as output tokens](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) . Fast became[the default in October 2026](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/release-notes) .


## How It Depends on LookML, and Where That Breaks


Because[Looker composes the query](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) , joins, access grants and user attributes apply as they do in an Explore. The price is that the agent only reaches what your model exposes. These limits surprise LookML developers:


-


**Custom fields and table calculations are invisible.** Google says[business logic kept in them is inaccessible](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-best-practices) . Promote the common ones into LookML.


-


**No pivots.** Multi-dimension results come back in long format, and verified queries[can’t contain pivots or custom fields](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-data-agents) either.


-


**Filter-only fields can’t be set.** The docs say the feature[cannot set the value of a field defined with the](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview)`[parameter](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview)`[or](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview)`[filter](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview)`[parameters](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) . In practice, expect trouble with Explores built around metric selectors or templated filters, where Liquid needs a user-chosen value. Test these first.


-


**Single-chart questions.** Trends, breakdowns, top values and single metrics work. Forecasting, correlation and anomaly detection are[outside the standard path](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) . Advanced Analytics covers some of this with Python, but only in data agents, and[not on Google Cloud core instances using CMEK or VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/looker-core-feature-differences) .


-


**50,000 rows per query.** That’s the[documented cap](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) .


> Your LookML is now prompt context with a price on it. Every exposed field description is input the model reads, so hiding fields improves answers and cuts the bill at once.


The feature[fetches the Explore schema at the start of a request](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) , and[LookML metadata counts as input tokens](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) . Google’s advice on[field bloat](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-best-practices) is to hide keys and technical fields, and to consider an agent-specific Explore built with` extends` . It also warns that free-form instructions go stale, and recommends verified queries,[no more than 30 to 50 per agent](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-data-agents) .


Governance has two gaps worth raising with security early.[By default, raw prompts and responses aren’t recorded](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/gemini-overview-looker) in System Activity or Cloud Logging; admins see them only through a preview feature, for users who consent. Admins also can’t bulk-delete history or set a retention period. Separately, the feature[isn’t yet in the FedRAMP High or Medium boundaries](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) .


## Looker vs Looker Studio: Conversational Analytics in Data Studio


[Looker Studio went back to the name Data Studio in April 2026](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/welcome) , and[Google’s docs now say](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/conversational-analytics-overview) “Gemini in Data Studio (née Gemini in Looker)”. So an older page about “Gemini in Looker” may describe a different product. The two share a feature name and little else:


-


**Looker** is the paid platform. Its chat is grounded in LookML, on[both Google Cloud core and Looker (original)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-overview) . Looker (original)[must be Looker-hosted for Gemini features](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/gemini-overview-looker) .


-


**Data Studio** has[two experiences](https://docs.cloud.google.com/data-studio/conversational-analytics-overview) . The new one is open to all users, but only talks to data agents built in BigQuery and shared to Data Studio.


-


**Legacy Data Studio chat** handles CSV, Sheets, Looker and BigQuery sources, and needs a[Data Studio Pro subscription](https://cloud.google.com/looker-studio) at $9 per user per project per month. Legacy agents and conversations can’t be migrated, and Google says the switch stays available only “for a time”.


The trap:[Looker data sources aren’t supported in the new experience](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/conversational-analytics-looker-studio) . A team chatting with Explores from Data Studio today should plan to rebuild those agents in Looker before legacy goes away. Also,[complimentary Data Studio Pro licenses aren’t available](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/release-notes) for Google Cloud core instances created after August 1, 2026.


## Looker Conversational Analytics Pricing From February 2027


You need Looker first. Google’s[pricing page says call sales](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) , though its[SKU list](https://cloud.google.com/skus?filter=looker&currency=USD) shows Standard edition at $5,000 and users at $30, $60 and $125. The list states no billing period. Our[Looker pricing guide](https://upsolve.ai/blog/looker-pricing) treats Standard as about $5,000 a month, and the[detailed breakdown](https://upsolve.ai/blog/looker-pricing-detailed-breakdown) covers the rest of the platform.

Tokens pool across the instance, reset monthly and don’t roll over. Standard edition is[for fewer than 50 users](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) , so it always sits on the floor. The floor equals 60 internal users, or 240 embed users.


### The meter has already changed twice


Pages written a few weeks ago can be wrong:


-


**May 2026:**[per license type](https://web.archive.org/web/20260516215114/https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) (Viewer 1M, Standard 2M, Developer 4M input), billing from October 1, 2026.


-


**August to October 2026:**[per subscription tier](https://web.archive.org/web/20261001061147/https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) (Standard 60M, Enterprise 300M, Embed 1.2B input). By late September the October date had gone, replaced by a promise of 90 days’ notice.


-


**November 2026:** per activated user with a floor, billing from February 1, 2027.


None of these allowances has been billed. But the current model shifts allowance from small instances to large ones, and hits small embedded deployments hardest.


An Embed instance with 500 embed users and 20 internal users went from 1.2B input tokens to 145M, about 88% less. An Enterprise instance with 100 users went from 300M to 100M. With 500 users it rose from 300M to 500M.

At modest token use, overage is small next to the platform fee. On these assumptions output runs out first for internal teams, because the allowance ratio is 50:1. And the result swings hard with tokens per question, so that number matters more than the rate.


Don’t guess it. The[token usage tab in System Activity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/system-activity-dashboards) shows estimated tokens by agent, user and conversation, refreshed every 24 hours. You have until January 31 to measure a real number.


Two other meters sit beside this one:


-


**Your warehouse.** Answers run as real queries, and[sampling values and fuzzy search can add database load](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-best-practices) . Hard-code` suggestions` or point` suggest_dimension` at something cheap.


-


**API quotas.** The[Looker-managed MCP server](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/mcp) costs nothing extra, but agent tool calls consume API quota, and[Standard edition includes 1,000 query-based API calls a month](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) . An MCP-connected agent could use that up quickly.


## When a Dedicated Data Agent Fits Better


Stay native if your important data is already modeled in LookML, your users work in Looker, and most questions fit a single chart. Governance is already in place, and buying another tool to avoid some model cleanup rarely makes sense.


A dedicated agent such as[Upsolve](https://upsolve.ai/pricing) fits better in four situations:


-


**The data isn’t in LookML.** Modeling comes first with Looker, and[each model can use only one connection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/reference/param-model-connection) . Google’s API docs describe multi-Explore questions as[separate queries compared afterward](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/known-limitations) , not joins. Upsolve[needs no existing semantic layer](https://upsolve.ai/) and works across Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift and Postgres at once.


-


**People want answers outside Looker.** Google documents Looker, iframes, its APIs and Gemini Enterprise (Preview). A chat agent in Slack or Teams means building on those APIs. Upsolve ships[a Slack agent](https://docs.upsolve.ai/slack/overview) , Teams, an SDK and MCP. MCP alone isn’t the deciding reason, since Looker’s managed MCP server went GA on October 26, 2026.


-


**The chat is part of your product.** Looker supports signed embedding, but it’s[iframe-based, requires a Looker-hosted instance, and applies only General theme options](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/conversational-analytics-looker-embedding) on the Conversations page. Upsolve’s Team tier adds an embedding SDK, multi-tenancy and row-level security.


-


**You want testing and traces in your own hands.** Looker offers verified queries, a preview pane and thumbs feedback. Upsolve’s[golden assets double as test cases](https://docs.upsolve.ai/ai-agent-builder/golden-assets) (tests are in beta), scored with LLM-as-judge, with[step-by-step traces](https://docs.upsolve.ai/ai-agent-builder/agent-observability) for each answer. Judge the results on your own questions.


Upsolve Team is $2,000 a month with 10,000 credits, about 1,000 analytical questions, and[overage is $0.05 per credit](https://upsolve.ai/pricing) . If your data and users already sit inside Looker, its chat is the natural default. A dedicated agent is worth paying for when it reaches data and users Looker doesn’t. For the wider field, see our[AI analytics tools roundup](https://upsolve.ai/blog/ai-business-intelligence-tools) and[Looker alternatives](https://upsolve.ai/blog/looker-alternatives) .

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is conversational analytics in Looker?


It’s a Gemini-powered chat feature that answers plain-English questions from your Looker Explores and dashboards. Gemini chooses the fields and filters, and Looker builds the query from LookML.


### Is Looker Gemini the same as Conversational Analytics?


No. Gemini in Looker is the full set of AI features, including the Visualization Assistant, LookML Assistant and Insight Assistant. Conversational Analytics is the chat feature within that set, and it’s the one with published token pricing.


### How much does Looker Conversational Analytics cost?


There are no token charges through January 31, 2027, within fair usage limits. From February 1, 2027, usage above your allowance costs[$3 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) , on top of your Looker subscription. Check the page before budgeting, since the terms have changed this year.


### Does Conversational Analytics work without LookML?


Not in Looker. It’s built on Explores, so someone has to model the data first. In Data Studio, the new experience uses BigQuery data agents instead, with no LookML involved.


### Can I use Conversational Analytics in Looker Studio?


Yes, under its new name, Data Studio. But the[new experience doesn’t support Looker data sources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/studio/conversational-analytics-looker-studio) . To chat with Explores, use Looker itself.
